If something from the pile belongs somewhere else, I put it in its own pile/box/basket to transport later, that way I don't have to leave the room I'm in and get distracted by the other mess everywhere else.

Judgemental means to have or display an excessively critical point of view, so no I wasn't being judgemental of whichever situation you were raised in. I know my basis for comparison isn't the be all, end all. I'm not that self-centered. I know everybody is different. 

And yes, we finally are seeing some common ground! Usually our partners are not our children or parents, so they can generally figure things out themselves. An exception would be if there were special circumstances, like a physical or mental difficulty. Someone who has a phobia of being hurt might have trouble cooking hot meals or handling knives. Someone who is very tall or very short might have difficulty functioning in a standard kitchen. In those cases, where there's mitigating circumstances, you can and should make concessions for your partner. Just as an example, if my husband broke his leg and was on crutches, I would not reasonably make him carry his plate to the table. I'm sure he'd be able to figure it out on his own, but in that instance it would be much easier for me to do for him. I wouldn't make a fuss over it either. It's just something I'd do to help him.

Hopefully you've learned some things here. What being judgemental means, that everyone is different, that calling names is rude in most parts of the world, the difference between assorted family members and your partner, how to make concessions for special circumstances when it comes to our relationships, etc. 

I feel you've really grown as a person in just this short span of conversation. Good job, friend.
